approachQuestion.prompt: Convert a valid expression of nonnegative integer operands, +, *, and parentheses to postfix tokens. Multiplication precedes addition; both are left-associative. Length<=200,000. Return tokens preserving integer literals. Example "2+3*4" -> [2,3,4,*,+]; "(2+3)*4" -> [2,3,+,4,*]. Operands are decimal literals from 0 to 1,000,000,000; no unary operators exist. Whitespace is absent. Measure length n in characters, including all digits. Return a token array of integer values and operator symbols.

options.text: Emit operands immediately; hold operators and parentheses on a stack. Before pushing an operator, pop operators of equal or higher precedence; at close pop through the matching open; drain at end.
options.feedback: The two examples distinguish precedence from parenthesized grouping.

options.text: Parse the valid expression recursively into a syntax tree, then emit its postorder operands and operators as postfix tokens.
options.feedback: A recursive precedence parser and postorder emission also read and emit each token once; the syntax tree and call frames take linear storage, tying the iterative operator stack bounds.

options.text: Emit operators immediately as they appear.
options.feedback: Immediate emission puts + before the later * in 2+3*4, so it violates precedence.

options.text: Ignore all parentheses and convert using only multiplication-before-addition precedence.
options.feedback: For (2+3)*4 this returns [2,3,4,*,+] instead of [2,3,+,4,*], changing the grouping.

Pop equal-precedence operators too because the stated operators associate left to right. Parentheses block reductions until their matching close. Each operator waits on the stack once rather than triggering a rescan of the entire prefix.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For infix-to-postfix-operators-optimal, let n be the number of input commands or tokens. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Input is immutable; output storage is excluded.
constraints: Tokens are recognized in one left-to-right scan. Each operator is pushed once and popped at most once.
The returned postfix token array is output and excluded from auxiliary space; the operator stack counts.
No recursive parsing, substring copies, or whole-input rewrites are used.

Scan digits once per literal; literals occupy one word under the stated bound. Return a fresh postfix token array. Its writes count in time but its storage is excluded. Iterative operator stack uses at most n entries.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Operators enter and leave the stack once while operands go directly to output.
details: Every token is scanned once and each operator is pushed and popped once. The operator stack may hold O(n) operators; returned postfix tokens are excluded from auxiliary space.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Deeply nested parentheses can retain a linear number of opening markers and pending operators, distinct from returned postfix tokens.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Every operator and parenthesis marker is pushed once and removed once; precedence pops consume earlier pushes.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A final token can affect the expression's postfix suffix, requiring all tokens to be read.
